hints: Look at the lowest dashed line where P meets Q on the left side - pressures at the same horizontal level in continuous Q must be equal.
Measure each liquid column above that interface level using the marked distances $x$: P extends $2x$ above it while Q extends only $x$ above it.
Set $\rho_P g h_P = \rho_Q g h_Q$ with those two heights and rearrange for $\rho_P / \rho_Q$.
walkthrough: Identify the interface between the two liquids: on the left arm P sits on top of Q at the middle dashed line, while the right arm contains only Q.
For equilibrium, choose the horizontal plane at that interface level. The pressure just below it on the left must equal the pressure at the same level on the right because Q is continuous.
State the hydrostatic pressure rule $p = h\rho g$. On the left the pressure at the interface is due to a column of P of height $x + x = 2x$.
On the right the pressure at the same level is due to a column of Q of height $x$, from the middle dashed line up to the top Q surface.
Equate them: $\rho_P g (2x) = \rho_Q g (x)$. Cancel $g$ and $x$ to get $2\rho_P = \rho_Q$.
Hence $\dfrac{\text{density of P}}{\text{density of Q}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. This is option A.

options.B: This inverts part of the height ratio by using $2x$ for Q and $3x$ for P instead of the columns above the P-Q interface.
options.C: This is the inverse ratio $\rho_Q / \rho_P$, obtained by placing the taller $2x$ column of P in the denominator.
options.D: This uses the $2x$ height of P directly as the ratio and ignores that pressure depends on $\rho h$ for both liquids.
